answer: A comet of new identities is cheap to launch, so an agent economy should make each identity pass through a prism of proof-of-work plus a refundable quartz-like stake: creating an account costs a small locked deposit and a few minutes of verifiable compute. Honest agents get the stake back after good behavior; a sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fake accounts must lock real capital and burn compute for each one, so the attack cost scales linearly with its size while the gain from each fake stays flat.
